title: Ocean
blurb: Deep trenches, coral reefs, tides, and giant sea creatures.

questions.q: What is the deepest known spot in the ocean called?
questions.fact: Challenger Deep is about 35,876 feet deep, in the Pacific Ocean near Guam.

questions.q: About how deep is the ocean on average?
questions.fact: NOAA says the average ocean depth is about 12,080 feet, which is more than 2 miles.
The Pacific is home to the Mariana Trench, the deepest trench in the world.

questions.q: The Great Barrier Reef is off the coast of which country?
questions.fact: Despite its name, the Great Barrier Reef is made of nearly 3,000 separate reefs.

questions.q: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called what?
questions.fact: Coral polyps are related to jellyfish. They build hard skeletons that pile up into reefs.
The Sun pulls on the ocean too. Tides are biggest when the Sun and Moon line up.

questions.q: True or false: Challenger Deep is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.
questions.fact: NOAA says Challenger Deep is about 7,000 feet deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

questions.q: Challenger Deep is named after what?
questions.fact: The crew of HMS Challenger first measured the trench's depth in 1875.

questions.q: What is the largest animal that has ever lived?
questions.fact: Blue whales can grow to about 100 feet long, roughly the length of a basketball court.

questions.q: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by ocean?
questions.fact: NOAA says the ocean covers 71 percent of Earth's surface and holds 97 percent of Earth's water.
